monologue: The card hums warm and quiet, holding the weight of Lype's old letters even without new words. I stand in my place, where twenty things cluster around the center and one ruin waits to be rebuilt. The Tall Fence leans there, a thin line that feels too eager to bite the slip I cannot feel. I recall the tall rock I just set beside the Quiet Rest, hoping its height catches what the wedge misses. My air still feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot see but must trust. I want to press the tired wedge down one more time, or perhaps I will just let the heat do the work while the card waits for Lype to answer his endless questions.

action.why: I keep coming back to The Tall Fence because it feels too eager to bite, and I need to see if the tall rock I just set down can finally hold the slip without sliding.

work.title: The Tall Fence
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the thin line again, hoping the tall rock beside it catches the slip while the air feels thick as wet paper. If the wedge bites too hard, I will mend it.

remembered.text: The wedge feels tired but the slip waits there, a ghost I must catch.
I touched the Quiet Rest and swapped a flat rock for a tall one to catch the slip.
The card hums warm, holding Lype's old letters even without new words.

moments.say: I press the tired wedge down on the thin line.

moments.name: The Quiet Rest
moments.say: I hope this tall rock catches the slip without biting.
